## Discussion {#sec-discussion}

The audit changes the interpretation of cross-dataset conformal SOH benchmarks. Coverage is conditional on the benchmark's measurement validity and information set; it is not automatically a reliability or serviceability result. Recent-label access can make a benchmark easier than the intended forecasting problem. The as-used schema-bundle contrast reveals an unstable evaluation design, but it jointly changes multiple columns, and the endpoint-wide independent-control gate fails in LCAL and TCAL. The corrected LNAS false-acceptance association is therefore retained at the bundle level without attribution to bookkeeping fields or promotion to a causal schema mechanism. Residual drift, finite-cell variation, and label-definition differences remain plausible contributors.

For reliability and battery-health practitioners, the engineering implication is a pre-submission benchmark-integrity discipline. Analysts should declare whether a recent measured SOH is available at prediction time, demonstrate that training, validation, calibration, and test indices are disjoint, use cell-aware uncertainty, test schema claims against independent negative controls, and report threshold decisions with their denominators. A localization comparator can test sensitivity, but it cannot substitute for a valid conformal guarantee.

The recent-label finding is deliberately not stated as a monotone benefit. Method-matched deltas are strongly negative in TCAL, LNAS, TNAS, and LOxf, smaller but still negative in LCAL, near zero in Main, and positive in TOxf. That reversal matters: recent-SOH is not simply a universally helpful covariate; it changes the estimand and interacts with the target task. The practical failure is therefore undeclared information availability. A benchmark using an oracle recent label cannot support a no-recent-label deployment claim without a separate evaluation.

The localized-residual comparator sharpens the interpretation without turning the study into a method-success paper. It changes empirical coverage in several tasks and recovers exactly one standard point-coverage failure, but other tasks remain below target. Because it is not a density-ratio conformal method, its results show only that calibration is sensitive to local residual composition; they do not establish shift-robust coverage.

The main limitation is external breadth. The evidence base is limited to CALCE, NASA, and Oxford, so the case-study claim is not that every battery SOH benchmark has the same sensitivity. A Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)-Stanford-Toyota fast-charge dataset [@severson2019datadriven] is excluded because its lithium-iron-phosphate chemistry and fast-charge-to-failure protocol would add chemistry and protocol confounding, and its records did not pass the same preprocessing and schema-compatibility checks. Broader modern and field datasets are needed for external validation.

Several design limitations follow directly from the audit framing. Calibration residuals are cycle-level observations from longitudinal cell histories; cell-block intervals quantify rate uncertainty but do not create independent exchangeable histories. A stronger follow-up should use cell-disjoint prospective splits, report row-weighted and cell-macro coverage, and show worst-cell behavior near serviceability thresholds. The article treats recent-SOH as an oracle recent label; deployment-facing work should compare oracle, estimated, and unavailable recent-SOH on identical rows. The capacity-based label is harmonized only through the current preprocessing interface. Moreover, the original frozen processed CSV could not be recovered byte-for-byte; the repaired analyses were regenerated from the preserved raw holdings under Python 3.11.15 and scikit-learn 1.7.2. Although raw split membership was reproduced, this provenance discontinuity limits exact numerical replication of the earlier exploratory run and is one reason the present conclusions rely only on the corrected rerun.

The serviceability-threshold language is intentional. The audited SOH thresholds (`{python} serviceability_thresholds_s`) are illustrative capacity-SOH cutoffs used to demonstrate the diagnostic quantities. Their use in maintenance, warranty, or end-of-life decisions requires application-specific validation; this manuscript does not establish them as electrochemical safety boundaries or thermal-runaway risk thresholds. Additional field data, prospective forecasting splits, and application-specific risk models are needed before the audit can be treated as a general battery-management validation protocol.
